title: RBAC v2 escalation scripts, SSO validation checklist, and support macro pack
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Purpose: Produce a concise, field-ready pack to empower support and on-call engineers to safely troubleshoot RBAC v2 permission failures, validate SSO/SAML connections, and quickly collect audit evidence for compliance requests. Scope: escalation scripts for common failure modes, SSO/SAML validation checklist, step-by-step audit-log retrieval, and ~10 support macros (Slack/Gmail/Helpdesk templates) that engineers can use verbatim. Out of scope: full RBAC policy redesign and UI changes. This ticket bundles docs + macro templates + quick checks to reduce time-to-first-action for paged incidents and high-severity SSO troubleshooting.
acceptance_criteria: A searchable KB page (Confluence) that contains the escalation scripts and SAML checklist is published
At least 10 support macros added to the oncall macros library and tested in staging
A short demo (10–15 min) for support/oncall scheduled and recorded
All steps have exact command examples and required log locations for audit evidence
Security review sign-off recorded in ticket comments
tasks: Draft escalation scripts for: permission denied (token vs policy), role inheritance mismatch, expired role bindings, cross-account role linking failures
Author SAML/SSO validation checklist with IdP and SP step examples (Okta/OneLogin/AzureAD) and expected SAML response fields
Document audit-log query patterns for AWS/GCP/Postgres/Redwood-logstore and standard evidence export steps
Produce 10 support macros: triage questions, data collection templates, user-facing remediation steps, escalation headers
Coordinate security review and add mitigation notes for macros that include sensitive commands
Runbook peer review with PM and Support lead, incorporate feedback
Publish Confluence page and link from Support KB and Console help
Record a 15-minute enablement video and attach to KB
support_macros_examples: Macro: RBAC-PERMISSION-REQUEST - Use this when user reports permission denied. Text: "Hi <user>, thanks for the report. Please confirm: (1) exact error text and timestamp, (2) the resource ARN or path, (3) your role name (from profile). We will check role bindings and audit logs and follow up within 2 hours."

Macro: RBAC-TEMP-ACCESS-GUIDE - Use when providing temporary access. Text: "We can grant a scoped temporary role for up to 4 hours. Please provide justification and scope. If approved, we will create role-binding RBAC-temp-<ticket> and notify you."

Macro: SSO-VALIDATION-INFO - Use when user reports login failure. Text: "Can you share the SAML response ID and the exact error page? If using an IdP (Okta/Azure), please capture the SAML trace (developer tools) and attach. See steps: 1) reproduce, 2) save SAMLResponse, 3) send to our SSO team."
Macro: AUDIT-EVIDENCE-REQ - Internal: "Collect: user email, timestamp, request-id, route, model-version, token-id. Attach raw audit export (JSON/CSV) and redact PII before sharing externally."
Macro: ESCALATE-RBAC-ONCALL - Internal header: "P0 RBAC failure impacting >1 customer: paging oncall + include initial checks (auth logs, recent policy changes, infra deploys)."
escalation_scripts:
Scenario: user gets 403 'permission denied' when calling generation endpoint
1) Collect: timestamp, request-id, user-id or org-id, exact API route.
2) Quick check: query audit store for request-id: SELECT * FROM audit WHERE request_id='<id>' LIMIT 1. If present, note principal and policy_version.
3) If audit shows 'denied by policy X', run: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/roles/<principal> to fetch bindings.
4) If bindings look correct, check token TTL: decode JWT header and exp claim. If token expired, respond with remediation steps to user.
5) If role-binding missing, escalate to IAM owner with header 'RBAC P0 Escalation' and include evidence export.
6) If systemic (many users/roles), toggle defensive fallback policy (read-only fallback) per emergency playbook and notify SRE

Scenario: cross-org role link failing after deploy
1) Verify deploy timeline using deploy-tracker dashboard and link to candidate commit.
2) Search audit logs for 'role-link-create' events and failures.
3) If a recent schema migration touched the binding table, coordinate rollback or data-migration hotfix with infra owner.
4) Preserve logs and escalate to security if there is any sign of malformed bindings or unauthorized changes
saml_validation_steps: Step 1: Reproduce the auth failure with a test account and capture browser network trace (SAMLResponse) and HTTP status codes.

Step 2: Decode SAMLResponse (base64) and inspect Assertion Issuer, Audience, Subject, NameID, Conditions (NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter), and Attributes. Expected: Audience matches SP entityID, NameID format matches configured type.
Step 3: Check assertion signature validity using our public certificate: openssl base64 -d -in saml.txt | xmlsec1 --verify --pubkey-cert-pem sp-cert.pem
Step 4: Confirm clock skew: compare IdP timestamp to our auth server within +/- 120 seconds. If outside, recommend IdP clock fix or allow configured skew for the SP temporarily.
Step 5: Inspect attribute mappings for role/organization claims. If missing, ask IdP admin to add attribute 'redwood_role' with exact value documentation.
Step 6: For intermittent failures, enable SAML debug logs on the SP for 72 hours and collect correlated audit events for analysis
audit_log_debug_steps: 1) Identify the canonical request-id from the user report or client logs.
2) Query Redwood logstore: /internal/audit/search?q=request_id:<id> and export full JSON payload.
3) If using managed cloud logs: run aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /redwood/audit --filter-pattern '\"request_id\":\"<id>\"' --start-time <ts-1min> --end-time <ts+1min>
4) Extract fields required for compliance: timestamp, principal_id, action, resource, decision, policy_version, token_id. Save as CSV with headers for legal requests.
5) Redact PII: run simple grep-based redaction or use redwood-redact tool before sharing externally
6) If evidence is missing (retention gap), escalate to logs-retention-owner and include retention window and customer-facing impact
rollout_plan: Week 1: Draft docs and internal review with Support and Security
Week 2: Add macros to staging macros library and run tabletop with oncall volunteers
Week 3: Publish KB, run 15-minute training, collect feedback, iterate
Emergency: if an incident occurs while rolling out, pause publishing and apply triage scripts internally first
training_plan: Create 10-slide deck covering: key RBAC failure modes, SAML validation demo, audit evidence collection steps
Record 15-minute video walkthrough and upload to KB
Invite Support and Oncall to 30-minute Q&A after first week
Add 2 quiz questions to onboarding for new oncall engineers to validate knowledge
